assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling of a single microwave photon to a superconducting artificial atom routine, and it is the architecture for dispersive readout, qubit coupling and multi-qubit gates in essentially every superconducting processor. The idea is original, the physics is clean, and the impact spans quantum optics, quantum information and sensing. It is closely tied to the superconducting-circuit work recognised in 2025 but is a distinct discovery: the engineered light-matter interface rather than macroscopic quantum tunnelling.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiments (Wallraff and Schoelkopf with colleagues) are the decisive contributions. Only three names are allowed per prize, so Steven M. Girvin, whose theoretical role was large, would be left out; the choice among the four is a genuine and unresolved allocation problem. I choose the experimental pair plus the theory lead of the proposal.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent laboratories over two decades, with a stable interpretation and wide technological adoption. Timing is mature, though the committee must weigh how soon after the 2025 award a closely related circuit topic should follow.
uncertainties: Which three of the four credited people should share the prize, given Girvin's theoretical contribution.
Overlap with the 2025 prize scope and possible perception of field concentration.
I am professionally close to this community (Chalmers, WACQT), so my assessment may be biased in favour of it and should be discounted by the committee accordingly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how to realise gates and quantum simulation with trapped ions, and the experimental programme of Blatt and others demonstrated high-fidelity gates, entanglement of many ions and digital and analogue simulation. It is the best-established route to quantum information processing besides superconducting circuits, with a clear conceptual-to-experimental arc.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal in 1995; Blatt led the early experimental realisation of the gate and subsequent scaling. David Wineland was recognised in 2012 for ion control, so the new prize would concern computation and simulation specifically. Other experimentalists (for example in the NIST and Innsbruck-Oxford communities) also contributed, which makes the experimental share not entirely settled.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across several groups and by commercial platforms; the foundation of the field has been stable for roughly thirty years. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and the extent to which new laureates would be seen as distinct.
Whether other experimentalists deserve credit alongside Blatt.
Cirac and Zoller are also credited in other candidates, so double recognition should be handled in the final configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states, a prediction followed by clean experimental confirmation. Importance, originality and conceptual clarity are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction and introduced the Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. M. Zahid Hasan led the three-dimensional topological-insulator observations and also has a strong claim, and the BHZ theorists are not in the credited names. Allocating credit among theory, 2D and 3D realisations is therefore difficult.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with extensive independent confirmation, and Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz (2016) recognition of topological matter did not cover this. Timely.
uncertainties: Hasan versus Mele or Molenkamp as the third or second laureate.
The BHZ proposal is missing from the credited names, leaving a gap in the attribution.
Early topological-insulator work overlaps conceptually with the 2016 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle flat-band prediction and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the whole field of moire quantum matter. The theoretical prediction was sharp and quantitative and the experiment confirmed it, which is a classic Nobel pattern.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction of flat bands at a magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. Other experimental groups (for example Dean, Young, Yazdani and the Cao-Fatemi work with Jarillo-Herrero) are involved, but within the supplied credited names the configuration is reasonably supported.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and widely, though the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism remains open and the field is still moving. Recognition is somewhat early but defensible for the established core.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved.
Experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero, who is the only experimentalist in this list.
Some reproducibility and sample-dependence issues noted in the early literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction, fault tolerance and topological codes are the theoretical basis for scalable quantum computing, and as someone working towards error-corrected processors I judge the importance to be very high. Shor's code and the fault-tolerance threshold ideas, Steane's CSS-type codes and Kitaev's toric code and anyon-based approach are original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently introduced the first quantum codes in 1995-96; Kitaev proposed topological codes and fault-tolerant computation with anyons. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Aharonov, Ben-Or and others also made decisive contributions, so a three-person selection is partly arbitrary. Shor's factoring algorithm is a separate discovery and should not be conflated.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations of below-threshold logical qubits and error-corrected memories are now appearing in several platforms, so empirical confirmation is growing but still incomplete. A Nobel Prize for the theory may be slightly early compared with a full demonstration.
uncertainties: Large field of contributors beyond the three credited names.
Experimental confirmation of scalable fault tolerance is still developing.
Whether this is a physics discovery or primarily computer science and mathematics for the committee's purposes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattices realised the Hubbard model with ultracold atoms, including the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and single-site quantum gas microscopy, and made controlled quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter possible. Scientific value is high and general across many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposals (Jaksch, Zoller and others) and experiments (Greiner, Bloch, Esslinger, with Hansch also involved) split the credit. Five names are credited and only three may be chosen; I take the experimental leaders and note that Cirac and Zoller are better placed with candidate B006.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced in many laboratories. Timing is good, though the 2001 and 2018 prizes on cold atoms and lasers sit nearby.
uncertainties: Choice among three experimentalists and the theorists.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes.
Quantum-simulator results beyond classical reach are still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable Rydberg-atom tweezer arrays enabled large-scale quantum simulation, exploration of exotic phases and high-fidelity gates, and they have become a leading quantum computing platform. The impact is large, with rapid recent progress on logical qubits.
assessment.attribution: Lukin's group demonstrated large programmable arrays and many-body phases, Browaeys and others realised parallel experiments, Saffman proposed and demonstrated neutral-atom gates, and Zoller and Grangier contributed foundational theory and early blockade experiments. A fair three-person configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple groups, yet the field is young and still moving quickly; recognition would be early compared with ions and optical lattices.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the more established platforms.
Allocation among five credited names including theory pioneers.
Scalability beyond current demonstrations remains to be shown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of quantised conductance in quantum point contacts in 1988, found independently in Delft/Philips and Cambridge, is a clean and fundamental mesoscopic result that underpins quantum transport and later electron-spin and charge qubit work. It sits in the field of my own early research, so I recognise its significance first hand.
assessment.attribution: The two groups (van Wees and van Houten at Delft/Philips with colleagues, and Wharam, Pepper and co-workers at Cambridge) reported the effect almost simultaneously. The credited names support a three-way split, but Wharam and Thornton are missing, and Landauer's conductance formula is foundational theory.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature and universally confirmed. The delay in recognition makes timeliness questionable, and the Nobel significance may be viewed as tied to later achievements.
uncertainties: Missing co-authors and the role of Landauer's theory in the credit.
Whether the effect is judged an instrument-level finding or a discovery of Nobel size.
Possible bias from my own mesoscopic background.
